about.title: Arcata Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Arcata is a small city, but the products its residents use every day come from national and international supply chains — vehicle parts, farm and forestry equipment, household appliances, tools, and consumer goods. When one of these products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the person hurt may have a claim against the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer under California's strict liability rules. That means the injured person generally doesn't have to prove anyone was negligent — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. If a defective product injured you or someone you love in Arcata, the first steps matter: keep the product, note where and when it was purchased, and get medical care documented. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself, but we can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in the area who evaluates product liability cases and works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters for Arcata Residents

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, an injured person may not need to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was flawed and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers who sold the product can potentially be held liable, which widens the pool of parties an attorney can investigate.

items.title: Preserving the Product Preserves the Claim
items.desc: Since the defect itself is central evidence, keeping the product intact and unaltered after an injury can be critical to how an attorney builds your case.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach to product defects, you generally need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, not that the company was careless. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain how this applies to your case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, if you can do so safely. Don't repair, discard, or alter it, since the product itself is often key evidence in a defect case. Store it somewhere safe and let an attorney advise you on next steps.

items.question: Is this only for products bought in Arcata stores?
items.answer: No. Whether you bought the item locally along a corridor like Samoa Boulevard or H Street, ordered it online, or received it as part of equipment used for work or recreation around Humboldt County, a defective product claim can apply regardless of where the purchase happened.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
